secoes.corpo:
A functionality is the individual's ability to perform daily activities independently. In nursing, functional assessment is a central component of geriatric consultation, neurological rehabilitation, and hospital discharge planning. It determines the degree of assistance needed, eligibility for rehabilitation programs, and recovery prognosis.

O Barthel Index , created by Mahoney and Barthel in 1965, is the most widely used functional scale in the world. It assesses 10 Activities of Daily Living (ADL) — feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, transfers, ambulation, and stairs — generating a score from 0 (total dependence) to 100 (complete independence). Its simplicity, reproducibility, and sensitivity to change make it the instrument of choice in rehabilitation clinical trials.

Functional assessment not only documents the patient's current status but also allows monitor progress — a change of 5-10 points on the Barthel is considered clinically significant. The score directly correlates with length of hospital stay, need for institutionalization after discharge, and mortality in the elderly.

Introduction to Functional Assessment
A functionality is the individual's ability to perform daily activities independently. In nursing, functional assessment is a central component of geriatric consultation, neurological rehabilitation, and hospital discharge planning. It determines the degree of assistance needed, eligibility for rehabilitation programs, and recovery prognosis.

O Barthel Index , created by Mahoney and Barthel in 1965, is the most widely used functional scale in the world. It assesses 10 Activities of Daily Living (ADL) — feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, transfers, ambulation, and stairs — generating a score from 0 (total dependence) to 100 (complete independence). Its simplicity, reproducibility, and sensitivity to change make it the instrument of choice in rehabilitation clinical trials.

Functional assessment not only documents the patient's current status but also allows monitor progress — a change of 5-10 points on the Barthel is considered clinically significant. The score directly correlates with length of hospital stay, need for institutionalization after discharge, and mortality in the elderly.
